LESSON: WRITING 6.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING: PICTORIAL COMPOSITION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.4: Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing: Pictorial Composition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing: Pictorial Composition, part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we enjoy looking at pictures? 2. What messages do pictures communicate?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. choose possible topics for pictorial compositions,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing: Pictorial Composition in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. create a composition based on the visuals or pictures,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing: Pictorial Composition in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. judge visuals appropriately for creativity in writing. Learners is guided to: • Interpret pictures collaboratively with peers. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech application or point/sign or write to interpret. • Match the pictures with the different parts of a composition: beginning, middle and end. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or be supported by peers or learner support assistants to match 1. Why do we enjoy looking at pictures? 2. What messages do pictures communicate? 54 • Watch a variety of animations, videos and sample write pictorial compositions collaboratively with peers, Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are ensitive to light. • Arrange different pictures logically to write a story coherently, Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or be supported by peers, learner support assistants or the scribe to write. • Write a pictorial composition of about 120 -160 words, 55 • Proof read the pictorial composition, • Display their compositions in the classroom. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or be supported by peers to display.

4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
